facts.fact_text: In April 2003 a group of farmers held a demonstration in front of the Seimas (the Lithuanian Parliament) building.
The April 2003 demonstration was held to protest about the situation in the agricultural sector with regard to a fall in wholesale prices for various agricultural products.
The April 2003 demonstration was held to protest about the lack of subsidies for producing agricultural products.
The farmers demonstrating in April 2003 demanded that the State take action regarding the situation in the agricultural sector.

At the 16 May 2003 meeting of the Chamber of Agriculture, it was decided to organise protests in three different locations next to trunk roads in Lithuania to draw attention to problems in the agricultural sector.
Mr Bronius Markauskas and Mr Arūnas Kudrevičius were accused of incitement to riot under Article 283 § 1 of the Lithuanian Criminal Code.
The prosecutor noted that Mr Bronius Markauskas had taken part in the farmers' meeting of 16 May 2003, at which the farmers had decided to hold demonstrations near major highways on 19 May 2003.
The prosecutor noted that at the 16 May 2003 meeting, the farmers had decided that should the Government not grant their requirements by 11 a.m. on 21 May 2003, they would blockade those highways.
The prosecutor noted that on 19 May 2003 Mr Bronius Markauskas had told the farmers to blockade the roads on 21 May 2003.
The prosecutor noted that as a result of Mr Bronius Markauskas's incitement, at 12.09 p.m. on 21 May 2003 around 500 farmers had gone on to the Vilnius-Klaipėda highway.
The prosecutor noted that the farmers had refused to obey police requests not to stand on the Vilnius-Klaipėda road.
The prosecutor noted that as a consequence of the blockade of the Vilnius-Klaipėda highway, traffic had been blocked until 1 p.m. on 23 May 2003.
The prosecutor noted that traffic jams had occurred on neighbouring roads and road transport in the region had become impossible as a result of the blockade of the Vilnius-Klaipėda highway.
On 29 September 2004 the Kaunas City District Court found the applicants guilty of having incited riots or having participated in them, under Article 283 § 1 of the Lithuanian Criminal Code.
The five applicants were each given a sixty-day custodial sentence (baudžiamasis areštas) by the Kaunas City District Court.

The Kaunas City District Court suspended the sentences of all five applicants for one year, finding there was reason to believe that the aim of the punishment could be achieved without actually depriving them of their liberty.
On 25 October 2000 the Lithuanian Criminal Code was published in the Official Gazette (Valstybės žinios).
Article 283 § 1 of the Lithuanian Criminal Code establishes criminal liability for rioting, which is categorised as a public order offence.

Article 283 § 1 of the Lithuanian Criminal Code provides that a person who has organised or provoked a gathering of persons to commit public acts of violence, damage property or seriously breach public order in other ways, or a person who, during a riot, has committed acts of violence, damaged property or seriously breached public order in other ways, may be sentenced to a custodial sentence (baudžiamasis areštas) or imprisonment for up to five years.

The Supreme Court found that the applicants had been sentenced for their crimes under a law which had been valid at the time at which the crimes had been committed and their sentences had been imposed in accordance with the provisions of the Lithuanian Criminal Code.
On 29 September 2004 the Kaunas City District Court found the applicants guilty of having incited riots or having participated in them, under Article 283 § 1 of the Lithuanian Criminal Code.
In convicting Mr Bronius Markauskas, the Kaunas City District Court relied on video recordings of the events, documentary evidence and the testimony of one witness.
The Kaunas City District Court concluded that Mr Bronius Markauskas had organised a gathering with the aim of seriously violating public order, that is to say a riot.

The Kaunas City District Court found that Mr Bronius Markauskas had been one of the leaders of the farmers' meeting on 16 May 2003, at which the farmers had decided to attempt to achieve their goals by organising protests next to trunk roads.

The Kaunas City District Court found that Mr Bronius Markauskas had coordinated the actions of the farmers and as a consequence on 21 May 2003 around 500 people had gone to the Vilnius-Klaipėda road and had blocked it.
The Kaunas City District Court found that as a result of Mr Bronius Markauskas's actions, car traffic on the Vilnius-Klaipėda road had been blocked until 23 May 2003.
The Kaunas City District Court found that the ensuing serious breach of public order had been deliberate and had to be qualified as rioting.
The Kaunas Regional Court found that the actions of Mr Bronius Markauskas and Mr Arūnas Kudrevičius had caused damage to goods carriers and had thus seriously breached public order.

The Kaunas Regional Court found that by driving tractors on to the road, causing traffic congestion and disturbing the work of the State border control service, and by refusing to obey lawful requests by the police not to park their tractors on the road, Mr Virginijus Mykolaitis, Mr Kęstutis Miliauskas and Mr Artūras Pilota had seriously breached public order.

The Kaunas Regional Court found that the fact that after the roads had been blocked the police and the drivers had negotiated with the farmers with the result that some of the drivers had been let through did not diminish the danger of the offence and its unlawfulness.

The Kaunas City District Court found that the farmers had had another alternative, namely bringing complaints before the administrative courts, which the farmers had themselves mentioned during the meeting of 16 May 2003.

The Kaunas City District Court noted that under Article 31 § 2 of the Lithuanian Criminal Code, a person who created a dangerous situation by his or her actions could only rely on the defence of necessity when a dangerous situation arose through negligence.
The Supreme Court shared the appellate court's view that the applicants could not be considered as having acted out of necessity.

The Supreme Court held that the fall in milk purchase prices and other problems with subsidies for agriculture had not constituted a clear or present danger to someone's property, because the property in question had not yet materialised.
The Supreme Court held that the law protects existing property and that the State had not deprived the applicants of their property.
The Supreme Court held that the applicants' dissatisfaction with the Government's agricultural policy had not justified the acts for which the five applicants had been convicted.
In May 2003 the Kalvarija municipality issued a permit to hold a peaceful assembly in Kalvarija town, 'near the marketplace'.
In May 2003 the Pasvalys municipality issued a permit to hold a demonstration 'at the car park at the sixty-third kilometre of the Via Baltica highway and next to that highway'.
In May 2003 the Klaipėda municipality issued a permit covering an 'area in Divupiai village next to, but not closer than twenty-five metres from, the Vilnius-Klaipėda highway'.
Mr Bronius Markauskas was informed that he had to observe the law and to adhere to any orders from the authorities and the police in connection with the permitted gathering.
